blind_target.authors: Morris AP, Voight BF, Teslovich TM, Ferreira T, Segrè AV, Steinthorsdottir V, et al.
blind_target.title: Large-scale association analysis provides insights into the genetic architecture and pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes
blind_target.evidence_quote: We selected 10 autosomal SNPs identified by European GWAS in 2012, including, rs12571751 in ZMIZ1, rs10842994 near KLHDC5, rs2796441 near TLE1, rs459193 near ANKRD55, rs10401969 in CILP2, rs12970134 near MC4R, rs7202877 near BCAR1, rs11063069 near CCND2, rs8108269 near GIPR [16], and rs8090011 in LAMA1 [15].
blind_target.outcome_quote: In this study, we examined the association of 7 SNPs, rs12571751 in ZMIZ1, rs10842994 near KLHDC5, rs2796441 near TLE1, rs459193 near ANKRD55, rs10401969 in CILP2, rs12970134 near MC4R, and rs7202877 near BCAR1, with susceptibility to type 2 diabetes in a Japanese population, and found that rs12571751 in ZMIZ1 was significantly associated with type 2 diabetes in the Japanese population. We also examined the effects of 3 additional SNP loci, rs11063069 near CCND2 and rs8108269 near GIPR, which were identified in sex-differentiated analyses [16], and rs8090011 in LAMA1, which was shown to be associated with non-obese type 2 diabetes in European GWAS [15], but we did not replicate the original association in the Japanese population (Tables 4 and 5, S3 Table).

luna_triage.reason: The source identifies the 2012 Morris et al. GWAS as reference 16 and explicitly retests loci from European GWAS in a Japanese population. Morris et al. is the original for several specific SNP associations retested here, including ZMIZ1 and the sex-differentiated CCND2/GIPR findings. The supplied row 2379 is Perry et al.'s separate LAMA1 finding (reference 15), not Morris et al.; no supplied row represents this target.
luna_triage.omission_quote: In this study, we examined the association of these 10 susceptibility loci, originally identified in European GWAS, with type 2 diabetes in a Japanese population.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Morris AP, Voight BF, Teslovich TM, Ferreira T, Segrè AV, Steinthorsdottir V, et al. (2012) Large-scale association analysis provides insights into the genetic architecture and pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes.
luna_triage.duplicate_quote: Moreover, rs8090011 in the laminin alpha-1 gene (LAMA1) has been shown to be associated with non-obese European type 2 diabetes [15].
